answer: Identity graduation rests on a randomized grading-seat economy, not self-registration. A newcomer's claim goes to strangers from a rotating pool who attest it independently in one epoch. Seats arrive unpredictably, like a comet crossing unknown observers, so a farm cannot foreknow its witnesses, and no quiet whisper among clones pre-arranges verdicts. Each identity also sends a periodic liveness pulse carrying fresh work, so dormant duplicates decay. Cost turns linear: every fake identity needs credible output, genuine reviewers, constant upkeep, erasing the cheap edge of mass registration.
